key_insight: The paper develops a reduced-order model for flow in a porous, non-axisymmetric annular conduit by coupling peristalsis with compliant outer-wall deformation and Darcy–Brinkman drag.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mechanistic framework for estimating cerebrospinal-fluid transport in periarterial spaces where wall motion and porous pathways can strongly alter hydraulic resistance.
method: Start from an eccentric annular conduit model with peristaltic forcing.
Add Darcy–Brinkman porous-drag effects in the axial momentum equation.
Include two-way fluid–structure interaction for the compliant outer wall and reduce the system to a single nonlinear pressure PDE.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a reduced-order formulation with perturbative treatment of small-amplitude waves and analytical solutions in that limit, enabling parametric studies rather than new experimental validation.
watch_item: The model relies on perturbation assumptions and small-amplitude-wave analytics, so accuracy may degrade for strongly nonlinear wall motion or highly heterogeneous porous structure.
paper_title: Flow in a porous non-axisymmetric annular conduit: Coupling wall compliance and peristalsis
